subject: Educational Psychology
stem: When a child misbehaves, the teacher removes them briefly from an engaging classroom activity to a quiet, unstimulating corner, temporarily withdrawing access to reinforcement (peer attention, participation). This specific negative-punishment technique is called:
explanation: Time-out works by temporarily removing a child's access to reinforcing stimuli (attention, activity) following misbehaviour — a form of negative punishment — distinct from a token economy (an ongoing reward-token system) or shaping (reinforcing successive approximations toward a target behaviour).
